root_cause: Two regressions from the v14.3.0 rewrite of rich/cells.py. (1) #3947: _cell_len's ZWJ branch calls next(iter_characters) inside a for-loop, so a trailing '\u200d' (e.g. '\u200d', '1\u200d', 'a\u200d\nb' per line) raises StopIteration, which surfaces as RuntimeError when cell_len runs inside a generator (segment.py sum(...)). (2) #3950: get_character_cell_size now looks up the new unicode width table, which has no entries for C0/C1 control characters (the old _cell_widths.py had (1,31,-1),(127,159,-1)), so control chars fall through to the default width 1 instead of 0. The leftover 'return 0 if width == -1' branch is dead code, a hint that the old table was dropped.
best_solution: In get_character_cell_size, return 0 up front for control codepoints: `if codepoint and codepoint < 32 or 0x07F <= codepoint < 0x0A0: return 0` (NUL still resolves to 0 via the table), and tidy the binary search to `while lower_bound <= upper_bound` returning `width` directly. In _cell_len, replace the iterator plus next() with an index-based while loop: on '\u200d' do `index += 1` (skip the joined character, same semantics as before), then `index += 1` at the end of each iteration. Running off the end no longer raises. Keep the ZWJ-swallows-next-char behaviour, because the hidden test pins cell_len('1\u200d2') == 1 and the existing split_graphemes tests pin the grapheme spans.
acceptable_alternatives: Use next(iter_characters, None) or try/except StopIteration in _cell_len (v4/v7 did this and passed test_zwj). For control chars, a frozenset or range check anywhere before the table lookup, or adding (0,31,0)/(127,159,0) ranges to the table lookup, as long as cell_len(chr(i)) == 0 for i in 0..30 and printable ASCII still takes the _is_single_cell_widths fast path.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py::test_zwj: cell_len('') == 0, cell_len('\u200d') == 0, cell_len('1\u200d') == 1, cell_len('1\u200d2') == 1 (ZWJ still consumes the next char, no exception). tests/test_cells.py::test_non_printable: cell_len(chr(i)) == 0 for every i in range(31). The existing test_split_text / test_split_graphemes ZWJ-emoji cases must keep passing, so split_graphemes must not change.
locating_signals: Title 'Fix ZWJ and edge cases' says ZWJ, i.e. '\u200d'; grepping it leads straight to rich/cells.py _cell_len and split_graphemes. The functions are not named. The second requirement (control-character width 0) appears only in the linked issue #3950, and the statement text is just two issue URLs. In-repo hints: the dead 'width == -1' branch in get_character_cell_size, and git history showing the removed _cell_widths.py control ranges.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4 and v7 wrapped next(iter_characters) in try/except StopIteration (plus harmless split_graphemes clamps), so test_zwj passed, but they never touched control-character widths and failed test_non_printable (cell_len('\x01') == 1). v6 changed the semantics: it stopped skipping the char after ZWJ in _cell_len and changed split_graphemes' `index += 2` to `+= 1`, which broke 8 existing test_split_text/test_split_graphemes ZWJ-emoji cases and would make '1\u200d2' measure 2. v8 only added scratch files test_zwj.py/test_zwj_fail.py with no source change, so it failed test_zwj (StopIteration) and test_non_printable. Pod runs: v4 95s/43 calls, v6 40s/17, v7 68s/29, v8 374s/24.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement is just a title plus several 'Fixes #N' links, count each link as a separate bug, and read vague title words like 'and edge cases' as unmet requirements. If you cannot read the issue text, find the missing bug by diffing the rewritten function against its previous version in git log/history: special cases the old code had and the new code dropped (here, control chars measuring 0), and dead branches that no longer fire, are the usual regressions. When fixing a crash, keep the existing semantics (fix the exception, not the behaviour) and run the module's existing tests before submitting, since changing semantics broke pinned tests in one run. Never submit only scratch test files.
